post.summary: The explicit split-sync action that replaces the sync these read paths used to do
post.description:
silently (#50).

A POST, not a GET, because it writes: it fetches from the provider and inserts
`SPLIT` transactions. That is what gives a provider outage somewhere to be reported
— as a 503 with a retry hint, rather than as a 200 whose numbers are quietly
pre-split.

The per-asset throttle from #38 still applies, so this is cheap to call: an asset
synced within the window and whose history is still covered costs one indexed read,
not a provider round trip.

200.description: Synced; per-asset failures listed in the body

503.description: Every asset failed to sync — a provider outage

get.summary: The tax summary, or — with `from` and/or `to` — the dated tax report.
get.description:
Same route, same access level, two shapes. Without a window the response is the
summary object this endpoint has always returned, which carries `assets` with the
open lots the Holdings tab renders; it is not described here, and its shape is
deliberately unchanged (the printable statement and `PortfolioDetail` both read it).
With a window the response is `ReportResponse`.

No `params(...)` block, deliberately: the parameters come from the handler's own
arguments, which is why `strategy`, `threshold_days`, `from`, `to` and `format` are
all in the committed document without one. `?format=csv` (dated requests only) answers
the same bytes the JSON payload carries, as a server-generated file: the CSV is a
projection of `ReportResponse`, so no number in it is re-derived. It is described here
rather than as a second content type for status 200, which utoipa's response map —
keyed by status — cannot express.

200.description: Dated tax report when a window is given; the legacy summary object otherwise

422.description: Invalid window, or a price or rate does not exist at or before the window end

503.description: A pricing provider is unreachable, or the report exceeded its elapsed deadline

200.description: Realized P&L breakdown for the sell

AssetTotals.description:
One asset's dated totals. Every field is computed in Rust from the same replay that
produced the rows; no renderer sums anything.

price_date_used.description:
The close that priced this asset, and the date it actually came from. Null when
the asset has no transaction at or before the window end, so no close was needed.

split_applied.description: A SPLIT dated on or before the window end was applied to the lots in scope.

ErrorBody.description:
The one body every failure returns. Validation failures carry an empty pair of lists
and name the offending parameter in `error`; a pricing failure populates them.

missing_prices_total.description: How many were found, before the lists were capped. Truncation is never silent.

LotMatch.description:
One row per buy lot consumed by one sell. `buy_price` and `unit_cost` are
split-adjusted and expressed in the portfolio base currency; `unit_cost`
additionally carries the amortised buy fee.

term.description: "SHORT" | "LONG", populated for the HYBRID strategy only; null otherwise.

MissingRate.description:
One currency pair a rate could not be found for. A missing rate is a pair, not a
symbol, and the body says which it is.

splits_last_synced_at.description:
When the least recently synced asset in this portfolio last synced splits,
or `None` when any asset has never synced. `None` is not "long ago" — it means
no split has ever been looked up for every asset here, which the UI says in
those words rather than as an age. See #50: split sync is an explicit action
now, so a stale portfolio has to be visible rather than silently wrong.

PriceSource.description:
How the dated report priced an asset's close. Recorded so a regenerated file can
state where its numbers came from (Goal 4), and so a database-answered report can be
told from a provider-answered one.

ReportContext.description:
What a dated request was answered about. `ReportContext` is the single authority for
`strategy` and `threshold_days`: the response does not repeat them at top level.

requested_from.description:
The window actually applied, not the parameters as typed. `requested_to` is the
call's `to`, or today when `to` was absent; `requested_from` is the call's `from`,
or the portfolio's first transaction on or before `requested_to`, or `None` when
the portfolio has no transaction at all. An open end is visible in the artifact
rather than inferred by its reader.

splits_note.description:
Splits are as recorded when this was generated; the dated path deliberately does
not sync them (issue #50), so a split recorded after the fact changes past
figures. A constant string in the payload rather than prose in each renderer,
because the CSV carries it as a cell (the file's first row is the header row).

ReportResponse.description: The dated report: the run context, per-asset totals, the portfolio rollup and every row.

ReportRow.description:
One report row. Three selections share one shape: the kind-specific cells are null on
the rows where they do not apply, never omitted and never zero.

The asset-level pricing facts repeat on every row of that asset — one close per asset,
not one per lot — so the CSV is a projection of this vector and needs no join.

buy_price.description:
Split-adjusted, in the portfolio's **base** currency — converted at the buy's own
date. NOT `asset_currency`: `DatedLot.buy_price` and `LotMatch.buy_price` are both
`tx_price * get_rate(asset, base, buy_date)`, and the frontend already renders
`LotMatch.buy_price` with the base currency (`SellPnlModal.tsx:255`). The sell-side
price on the same row IS asset currency, so the two columns must not share a label.

cost_basis.description:
Sell-level, **matched quantity only**, in the portfolio's base currency. Summed
from the per-match figures; excludes the unmatched tail.

lot_pnl.description: The column that totals. `LotMatch.pnl` under the name the CSV uses.

proceeds.description:
Sell-level, **matched quantity only**, in the portfolio's base currency. Summed
from the per-match figures (`tax_engine.rs:761-763`), so it never includes the
unmatched tail and must not be added to the `lot_proceeds` of the sell's rows.

realized_pnl.description:
Sell-level, **matched quantity only**, in the portfolio's base currency:
`proceeds - cost_basis` over the matched lots. This is the whole sell's figure and
repeats on every `SOLD_LOT` row of that sell — the column to SUM is `lot_pnl`, not
this one.

sell_fee.description:
As entered, in `asset_currency` — same rule as `sell_price`, and the only other
field on this row that is not in the portfolio's base currency.

term.description: "SHORT" | "LONG" for HYBRID only; null otherwise, and never claimed on an open lot.

ReportTotals.description: The portfolio rollup: exactly the five per-asset figures, summed across assets.

RowKind.description:
Which selection a row is. Exhaustive on purpose: both renderers switch on it, and the
CSV's "this column totals, that one does not" rule is expressed through it.

SellPnlResponse.description:
Endpoint payload: the breakdown flattened next to the context needed to read
it honestly — which strategy produced it, which currency the money is in,
whether FX or a split touched it. `price`/`fee` are the raw as-entered values
in `asset_currency`; every other money field is in `currency`.

roi.description: Null when cost basis is zero — dividing there would invent a number.

split_applied.description:
A SPLIT on this asset dated on or before the sell: buy prices in the
matches are split-adjusted rather than as entered.

SyncSplitFailure.description: One asset whose split sync failed while syncing a whole portfolio.

failures.description:
Assets that could not be synced. A partial failure is still a 200 — the ones
that worked were written — and the caller shows this list. When *every* asset
fails the route answers 503 instead, because that is a provider outage and
retrying later is the only fix.

buy_transaction_id.description:
The buy that opened this lot. Present so a lot can be joined back to the ledger
row a person is reading.

pp_session.name: pp_session
pp_session.description: Session cookie issued by /auth/callback. There is no bearer token in this API: the browser never sees a credential.
